idiom_name: express-session with a compatible server-side store (connect-redis and friends)
implementation_notes: express-session is the de-facto Node realization: session(options) reads and writes the session cookie itself, keeps req.session on the server, and persists it through a store chosen with the store option, while resave and saveUninitialized decide when the record is written. The documentation is explicit that session data is not saved in the cookie - only the session id - and that the default MemoryStore is for debugging because it leaks memory and cannot scale past a single process, so production registers one of the compatible stores (Redis, MongoDB, a database) instead; cookie.path, cookie.httpOnly and cookie.sameSite are set deliberately because they are the whole attack surface of the identifier. There is no stdlib session, so the alternative to the middleware is reimplementing id signing, cookie attributes and a store interface by hand.
pitfalls: MemoryStore in production is the canonical failure: it leaks and does not span processes, so sessions disappear behind a load balancer (the docs' own warning).
cookie.secure and cookie.sameSite must be set explicitly - and a SameSite=None cookie is only valid together with Secure - otherwise the identifier rides on cross-site requests.
Changes are only visible on the next request: the middleware saves at response time, so a handler that mutates req.session then immediately re-reads it from a fresh request sees the old record.
